name: Waste Connections, Inc.
moat_justification: Permitted landfill airspace is scarce/irreplaceable, route density in exclusive/secondary markets, internalization rising, proven pricing power (core price +5.6% Q2 2026, +6.5% FY2025) and industry-leading ~33% adj. EBITDA margin, long municipal/franchise contracts — against larger WM/Republic bidders, rebid risk, no network effects, negative unit volumes, commodity/E&P cyclicality, and landfill closure/environmental liabilities (Chiquita Canyon). Sector flag fires on the screener's Utilities bucket; the business is contracted waste services, not a rate-regulated utility, but confidence is graded low per the sweep rule.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly; grade confidence low
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.2x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Strong-moat (7/10) waste compounder with real pricing power, but at $153.67 (TTM owner's earnings of $4.53/share, 2.95% yield) it yields a 7.11% weighted IRR — clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$52 (~$42 with a margin of safety); even the super-bull case ($105.57) is below today's price.
moat_for: Permitted landfill airspace is scarce and effectively irreplaceable; internalization captures the disposal margin
Route density in exclusive/secondary markets feeding owned transfer/disposal
Proven pricing power through cycles (core price +5.6% Q2 2026) with industry-leading ~33% adj. EBITDA margin
Long-duration municipal/franchise contracts give revenue visibility
Disciplined M&A machine in a fragmented industry
moat_against: No network effects; contracts rebid against larger WM and Republic
Landfill closure/post-closure and environmental liabilities (Chiquita Canyon)
Unit volumes negative; growth is price + M&A only
Recycled commodity prices and E&P waste volumes are cyclical
Capital intensity real and rising (RNG build-out, land purchases)
